content.title: About
content.content: Pepperoni pizza is a popular fast‑food option made with a thin, crispy crust, tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and slices of spicy pepperoni sausage. The pepperoni adds a distinctive aroma and mild heat, while the thin crust keeps the dish light and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “pepperoni” is Italian for “peppers,” but in the U.S. it refers to a spicy pork or beef sausage.
Thin‑crust pizza originated in Naples in the 19th century and became a staple of New York‑style pizzerias.
The combination of tomato sauce and mozzarella provides a good source of lycopene and calcium.
Pepperoni pizza is often considered a comfort food and is a common late‑night order.
In the United States, over 30 % of all pizza sales include pepperoni.

items.title: High in Protein
items.content: Pepperoni and cheese supply high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium Source
items.content: Mozzarella cheese contains calcium that supports bone and dental health.

items.title: Lycopene in Tomato Sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage and dough provide B1, B2, and B6 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick Energy
items.content: The thin crust and moderate fat content make this pizza a fast source of calories.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Pepperoni and sauce often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated Fats
items.content: Cheese and sausage add saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should choose a dairy‑free cheese alternative.

items.title: Spicy Food Sensitivity
items.content: Pepperoni may irritate the stomach of individuals with gastritis or ulcer disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pepperoni pizza is typically enjoyed hot, cut into slices. You can add fresh vegetables, basil, or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor. Some like to serve it with ranch or garlic dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crisp crust. It can be frozen for up to 2 months if wrapped tightly in plastic.
